preview.playersNote: Five Hurricanes and five Panthers who will decide Friday night.

intro.heading: The matchup
intro.body:
The Hurricanes come home hurting. Two straight losses have turned a **4-1** season into **4-2** and a first-place fight into a playoff scramble. The **40-24** second-half collapse against Collins was bad enough. Then Klein scored **22** unanswered after halftime in a **37-14** win that Dave Campbell's named one of its three big takeaways from Thursday night.

**Klein Cain (4-2, 2-2)** hosts **Klein Oak (2-4, 2-2)** on Friday, October 16 at 7 PM at Klein Memorial Stadium. The Panthers just hung **59** on Klein Forest in a 59-3 Friday night rout, and they arrive with momentum. On3's projection has Cain **38-34** with a **56%** win probability. With four games left and Klein and Collins separating at the top of **District 15-6A**, Cain needs this one to stay in the thick of the playoff race. *The bounce-back starts at home.*

The district table tells the story. **Klein (5-0)** and **Klein Collins (4-1)** sit at the top, Tomball is third at **3-1**, and Magnolia holds the fourth and final playoff spot at **3-2**. Cain and Oak are tied right behind at **2-2**, so Friday's winner moves to **3-2**, takes the head-to-head edge, and jumps into the playoff pack. The top four advance, and Cain's road stays in its own hands: Magnolia, the team in fourth, comes to Klein Memorial on October 29. And if Cain gets in, it goes **Division I**: at **3,784** students Cain is the largest school in the district, and the two largest qualifiers play in Division I.

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: Johnson leads Cain at **85.5** rushing yards per game with **nine** total touchdowns. The Bearkats bottled him up Thursday; he never found room against a front keyed on him all night. Friday is the reset: when Johnson gets going early, everything else opens up.

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: Hanks owns **eight** touchdown passes and **six** rushing scores, and his 35-yard touchdown run Thursday was Cain's brightest moment. But the Klein loss turned on his two interceptions and the empty red-zone trip. Take care of the ball first; the playmaking takes care of itself.

players.name: Gage Hansberger
players.tag: Cain's Player of the Game vs Klein
players.copy: Hansberger was Cain's Player of the Game against Klein: in on stops all night and the man who blew up the Bearkats' two-point try. The senior captain sets the tone for a front seven staring down a 4-star running back.

players.name: Christian Lovell
players.copy: Christian anchors the interior as a team captain. Oak's ground game runs through **Micah Rhodes**, all the more with quarterback **Andre Phillip II** out since mid-September and his Friday status unconfirmed; the fight starts with Christian's front winning the line of scrimmage.

players.name: Israel Smith
players.copy: Smith's **117**-yard night against Tomball showed what happens when the ball finds him. With defenses keying on Johnson, the perimeter is where Cain's big plays live.

players.name: Micah Rhodes
players.copy: The headliner. Rhodes is a 4-star recruit and 247 Sports' No. 8 running back in the 2028 class who committed to **Texas** on Oct. 8 after decommitting from Oklahoma in April. He ran for **229** yards and a score in Oak's 45-7 win over Tomball Memorial and holds 34 major offers. Cain has to know where **Micah Rhodes (#5)** is on every snap.

players.name: Andre Phillip II
players.copy: **Andre Phillip II (#2)** is the name on the marquee, but he may not be the quarterback Cain sees Friday. The **West Virginia** commit was Oak's dual-threat engine through three games: **95.7** rushing yards a game, **six** passing touchdowns and **three** rushing scores per MaxPreps. He has not played since, missing Tomball Memorial on Sept. 24 and Magnolia on Oct. 2, and no source has confirmed his status for Friday. Sophomore **Bryce Evins (#6)** has taken the snaps in his place, and Oak has used three quarterbacks this season. Cain has to prepare for both.

players.name: Antonio Dural
players.copy: Dural is Oak's No. 2 rusher behind Rhodes at **65.0** rushing yards a game per MaxPreps, with **four** rushing touchdowns. Pair him with Rhodes and the Panthers can attack both edges; fitting the run is job one Friday.

players.name: Carson Varro
players.copy: Varro is the top target outside: **45.0** receiving yards a game and **four** touchdown catches per MaxPreps. If Cain loads the box against the run, the Oak quarterback, whoever starts Friday, will look his way first.

players.name: Zack Ruysenaars
players.copy: Ruysenaars is the heart of the Oak defense at **11.0** tackles a game with **four** sacks per MaxPreps. Cain's line has to find him before Johnson does.

recruiting.heading: Klein Oak recruiting notes
recruiting.note: A roster-wide check of On3's Klein Oak prospect list, 247Sports coverage, and Rivals coverage as of Oct. 10 found two verified commitments on the current Panthers roster: junior running back **Micah Rhodes** committed to Texas on Oct. 8 after decommitting from Oklahoma in April, and senior quarterback **Andre Phillip II** has been committed to West Virginia since May 8, 2026. Reported offers are not commitments.

rows.name: Micah Rhodes
rows.note: The 2028 four-star running back committed to **Texas** on Oct. 8, flipping from Oklahoma (April decommit). SportCast Media cites 247 Sports' No. 8 running-back ranking; the 247Sports Composite has him No. 12 with 34 major offers. He ran for 229 yards and a score in Oak's 45-7 win over Tomball Memorial on Sept. 24.

rows.name: Andre Phillip II
rows.note: The senior QB is On3's No. 2-rated Klein Oak prospect (85.20), a dual threat with six passing and three rushing TDs per MaxPreps, all in Oak's first three games; he has not played since Sept. 11 and his status for Friday is unconfirmed. He committed to **West Virginia** on May 8, 2026, choosing the Mountaineers over Iowa State, Army, Air Force, and Navy.

rows.name: Quincy Carter
rows.note: The senior safety is On3's No. 3-rated Panther (84.23) with a caused fumble on MaxPreps.

rows.name: Max Farmer
rows.note: The 6-5, 285-pound junior lineman is On3's No. 4-rated Panther (82.33) with a sack and a caused fumble on MaxPreps.

items.title: Know where Micah Rhodes is
items.body: The 4-star **Texas** commit ran for **229** yards and a score against Tomball Memorial on Sept. 24 and holds 34 major offers. Fit the run, gang tackle, and make someone else beat you. **Gage Hansberger (#34)** and **Christian Lovell (#45)** set the tone.

items.title: Disrupt the quarterback, whoever it is
items.body: Oak's quarterback picture is unsettled: **Andre Phillip II** has not played since Sept. 11, and sophomore **Bryce Evins** has run the offense since. Either way the plan is the same: pressure the pocket, spy the quarterback run, and make a young passing game win on schedule.

items.title: Rebuild the run game
items.body: **Eyan Johnson (#16)** never found room against Klein, and the offense stalled with him. Oak's front is the reset button: establish the run early and **Jace Hanks (#9)** gets the play-action looks that produced **eight** touchdown passes.

items.title: Finish drives
items.body: The Klein loss had an empty red-zone trip, a missed **39**-yard field goal, and two interceptions. Friday, touchdowns have to replace field-goal tries.
